title: SpeechRouter WebSocket Protocol v0
description: Every JSON message on WSS /v1/listen and /v1/speak, discriminated by `type`. FRAMING: audio always travels as raw binary WS frames (client->server on /v1/listen, server->client on /v1/speak); ALL JSON events travel as text frames — a text frame is always an event in this schema, a binary frame is always audio. TIME BASE: every timestamp is audio-time seconds from the first audio sample of the session (not wall clock, not provider-native), monotonic across provider failover.

w.description: The word, punctuated/cased as the provider returns it

start.description: Audio-time seconds from first audio sample of the session; monotonic across failover (adapters apply the session offset)

speaker.description: Speaker index when diarization on; absent otherwise

lang.description: BCP-47, present only for multilingual models

SessionOpen.description: server->client, first message after WS accept

provider_raw.description: Optional passthrough of provider payload, only when ?include_raw=true

UtteranceEnd.description: Endpointing signal — the voice-agent trigger to respond

ProviderSwitched.description: Mid-stream failover happened; transcripts continue in same schema. DEDUP GUARANTEE: the gateway suppresses final transcripts from the new provider covering audio time already delivered as final — clients never receive duplicate finals for the same audio range. Interim events may re-cover replayed audio; standard interim semantics apply (superseded by the next final).

resumed_at.description: Audio-time seconds replayed from ring buffer

speaker_mapping_preserved.description: false: speaker indices reset with the new provider (client must treat labels as a new epoch). true: gateway aligned old/new labels via ring-buffer overlap and indices remain comparable. v1 always emits false; true is a forward-compatible upgrade.

TextDelta.description: client->server on /v1/speak: a chunk of text to synthesize. Text stays JSON (small); synthesized audio returns as binary frames.

Clear.description: client->server on /v1/speak: barge-in. Discard all queued/undelivered synthesis immediately; server responds with `cleared`. Essential for voice-agent interruption.

Cleared.description: server->client on /v1/speak: ack for `clear`. Chunks with seq <= last_seq are stale (client discards any it has buffered); chunks after belong to post-clear synthesis.

KeepAlive.description: client->server on either socket: hold the session open during audio/text silence. Needed because browser WebSocket API cannot send protocol-level pings. Send every ~8s of inactivity; sessions idle beyond the server's limit close with error audio_timeout.

AudioChunk.description: TTS /v1/speak server->client; audio itself travels as binary WS frames, this JSON frame precedes each with timing metadata

Finalize.description: client->server: flush and finish (STT) / end of text input (TTS)

code.description: Closed, stable set. REST endpoints wrap the same codes in an OpenAI-compatible {error:{code,message,type}} envelope.

recoverable.description: true = stream continues (e.g. failover in progress)
